text:
Brayden Schenn scored his 300th career goal in the first period, a backhander that put the Islanders up 2-0 in Nashville, and New York spent the rest of the night protecting a lead that kept shrinking. It was 3-0 early in the second before the Predators scored twice and then tied it on Ryan O'Reilly's backhand in the third. Kyle Palmieri and Bo Horvat each scored in the shootout, while Filip Forsberg and O'Reilly were both stopped, and NYI won 4-3. Palmieri, drafted 26th overall by the Ducks in 2009, was named first star without a point in regulation.

By our numbers, Nashville should have won. We put NSH's deserved-to-win figure at 58%, meaning the Predators win that share of simulated replays of every shot, and they led expected goals (the quality of chances) 4.34 to 3.86. The gap grew in the third period, when NSH out-chanced NYI 1.67 to 1.01. The Predators were also sloppier with the puck, with 19 giveaways to New York's six. Semyon Varlamov made the difference, saving 1.34 goals more than the chances against him should have allowed. His best stop came on Nils Hoglander, who had a 57% look in the second period.

Nashville's power play went 1 for 5, with Forsberg's second-period goal on the man advantage, and New York went 0 for 5. The Islanders leave with the extra point and a milestone for Schenn, while the Predators walk away with one point and the sense that the game was theirs to take.
